title: Cacik Yogurt Cucumber Dip

seo.h1: Authentic Turkish Cacik Yogurt Cucumber Dip Recipe

seo.imageCaption: Enjoy this refreshing and authentic Turkish Cacik, a perfect appetizer for any meal.

description: Cacik is a quintessential Turkish cold appetizer, a refreshing blend of creamy yogurt, crisp cucumbers, and fragrant garlic. This delightful dip is a staple on any mezze platter, offering a cool counterpoint to richer dishes. It's incredibly easy to prepare, making it perfect for a quick and healthy addition to your meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Cucumber
instructions.text: Wash and either grate the cucumber or finely dice it into small pieces. If grating, place the grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel or paper towels and squeeze out as much excess water as possible. This step is crucial to prevent the cacik from becoming watery.

instructions.title: Mince the Garlic and Chop Herbs
instructions.text: Peel and finely mince the garlic cloves. Finely chop the fresh dill. If using, prepare the dried mint.

instructions.title: Combine Main Ingredients
instructions.text: In a medium mixing bowl, add the strained yogurt, the prepared cucumber, minced garlic, chopped fresh dill, and dried mint (if using). Add salt to taste.

instructions.title: Mix and Add Olive Oil
instructions.text: Gently mix all the ingredients together until they are well combined. Stir in the 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.

instructions.title: Adjust Consistency (Optional)
instructions.text: If you prefer a thinner consistency for your cacik, gradually add cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing well after each addition until you reach your desired texture. Some prefer it thick, others slightly runnier.

instructions.title: Chill and Serve
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the cacik for at least 30 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully and ensures it is refreshingly cold. Before serving, drizzle generously with a little extra virgin olive oil and garnish with a sprig of fresh dill or a sprinkle of dried mint or paprika.

tips: Always use good quality, thick strained yogurt (süzme yoğurt) for the best creamy texture. Regular yogurt can be too thin and may make the cacik watery.
For a crispier texture and to prevent a watery dip, make sure to thoroughly squeeze out all excess water from the grated cucumber before mixing it with the yogurt.

Cacik tastes even better when chilled for at least 30 minutes to an hour, allowing the flavors to fully meld. Serve it cold, drizzled with extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of paprika or dried mint for garnish.
